No changes to existing helpers, tests, config, dependencies, deadlines or P2. JobProbe.cs copied
byte-for-byte from the preserved prototype; x64 Windows 10+, existing PowerShell 5.1 Add-Type.
The recorded execution uses installed Node 22.23.1, tsx 4.23.8, Git and Vitest 4.1.10.

- behavioral-baseline regeneration: each recipe has 31 Git commands and 12 explicit filesystem
  operations; each semantic snapshot has 10 Git commands. Two recipes plus snapshots: 82 commands,
  24 filesystem operations, 106 owner work registrations. Five refs and five snapshot commits
  preserve existing parallel queries. No worker extraction is part of this five-second test;
  the separate frozen-baseline extraction tests have an explicit 30-second deadline.
- fixture-lifecycle: fixtureIdentity is seven logical queries plus two persisted-config queries,
  with complete recursive file reads/hashes/lstat/readdir and statfs. prepare runs three identities
  and one recursive copy; capture runs two identities and two atomic evidence writes; finalize

  the queries/copy verification path is 73 (including initial/final identities and main rev-parse).

  Drift/marker/error cases stop earlier. Linux maintenance is outside Windows suitability.

## First failure and deterministic correction

First invocation failed before workload entry: --import received a Windows absolute path,
which Node interprets as c: protocol (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME). Peer stderr provides the
exact error; host has no inherited stderr pipe and reports missing workload receipt. First host
assigned its Node child, observed leader exit and zero count, then disposed the handle. This is
not successful workload evidence or a valid cold fit. First sources/logs/receipts are retained.
Only correction: use file URL in both driver launch sites. No recipe, bounds, load or compiler
change. Second invocation passed both finite assertions; all Git close receipts have code zero.

## Verdict and bounded next option

This is a lower bound: a single creation-time job encloses the entire Node driver. Git commands
use unchanged Node execFile inside that job, including actual argument/environment/cwd and capture.
It proves real Node/Git execution, spaced cwd and nested job compatibility in this host, not the
future host-mediated 82-command transport or individual jobs. Only one valid subsequent sample
remains after the setup failure. No valid cold sample, generic pipe-handle ownership, per-command
admission/cancellation or sealed final protocol has been established.

Do not infer an incremental per-command cost from the earlier 1,283.21 ms aggregate or add old
native launch timings to this total (that could double-count process work). The remaining 984 ms
is an untested budget for transport and its lifecycle barriers; practical full-boundary margin
has not been demonstrated. Stage A suitability is inconclusive; Stage B is withheld.

One bounded alternative for trunk: authorize a different command-batch test boundary that assigns
the whole helper recipe to one job and uses explicit file receipts, with its own cancellation,
failure and absence contract. It would avoid 82 host round trips, but arbitrary fixtureExec
commands/sidecar stdout remain blocked; existing helpers cannot be integrated on this evidence.
This alternative is neither implemented nor adopted. Do not repeat/tune this fit check without a
new scope decision.

Proposed eventual integration seam remains optional fixtureExec/owner and owned sidecar launch,
with Node retaining root/body/output settlement and requiring observed absence. Unix still needs
owned private-group observation after leader exit for normal and cancelled disposal. Neither
integration nor Unix correction is implemented. P1 and Windows PR readiness remain open.
